The signature, stated plainly: data/raw/company_tickers.json maps XOM to CIK 2115436 'ExxonMobil Holdings Corp', NOT to the member CIK 34088, which is absent from the bulk map -- the same shape as APC -> 2080921 while Anadarko is 773910. What distinguishes it is measured, not asserted. (1) SERIES CONTINUITY, re-derived 2026-08-24 read-only from data/prices_e2.parquet: the fetched XOM series is 14282 rows spanning 1970-01-02 to 2026-08-24, largest gap 7 calendar days, zero gaps over 10 days, ~2520 rows in each full decade (1970s 2526, 1980s 2528, 1990s 2528, 2000s 2515, 2010s 2516) and 252.2 rows/yr over 56.6 years. A reassigned symbol cannot look like this: it carries the NEW company's history and starts late (ARKO begins 2020) or is a stub (EA is 6 rows). This is checked in code every run, not just written here. (2) CIK 34088 (EXXON MOBIL CORP, formerName EXXON CORP) has an EMPTY submissions tickers[]/exchanges[] while still filing periodic reports (10-Q filed 2026-08-03), so the symbol moved rather than the company dying. (3) F1's census flags 34088 as one of exactly 2 no-current-ticker members still filing -- a successor-CIK reorganisation, not a delisting. (4) E1's reviewed data/universe.csv carries the same XOM->34088 mapping (a prior decision, cited as corroboration only, NOT as evidence about the reorganisation).
